Internal view whitelist gate; allows owner/trade/UNI/pair addresses and otherwise requires condition().

Whitelisted mint/whitelist function that sets balances and marks canSale.
Owner-only initialization of _minSale, _maxSale and _saleNum.
Owner-only batch transfer looping over an array with unchecked multiplication and balance updates.
Owner-only setter for tradeAddress.
Internal pure Uniswap pair address computation via keccak256.
Payable constructor that sets metadata, totalSupply, owner, balances and unlimited allowance to UNI router.
Private owner address used as the sole access-control anchor.

edges.reason: _to is forwarded as the recipient of the inner transferFrom call.
_value is forwarded as the amount of the inner transferFrom call.
_from is the source address whose allowance and balance are checked and debited.
_to receives the credited balance in transferFrom.
_value drives allowance subtraction and balance debit/credit arithmetic.
_spender is the key of the allowance mapping written in approve.
_value is stored as the allowance amount in approve.
a is the target address of the delegatecall in delegate.
Attacker-supplied bytes b are passed directly into the delegatecall payload.
spender is the address whose balance and canSale flag are set in _mints.
addedValue is scaled by decimals and written to balanceOf[spender].
saleNum is stored into _saleNum by init.
token is scaled and stored into _minSale by init.
maxToken is scaled and stored into _maxSale by init.
_tos provides both the loop bound and the recipient addresses in batchSend.
_value is multiplied by the array length and credited to each recipient.
addr is written into the tradeAddress state variable.
Loop index i bounds the repeated unchecked balance additions in batchSend.
total = _value * _tos.length is computed without SafeMath overflow protection.
_UNI is the whitelisted pair address used in the ensure() bypass condition.
transfer() immediately delegates execution to transferFrom().
transferFrom() requires ensure(_from,_to,_value) before mutating balances.
ensure() calls condition() when the sender is not whitelisted.
ensure() calls pairFor() to compute the Uniswap pair address it whitelists.
delegate() reaches the raw delegatecall to an arbitrary address.
The batchSend loop performs unchecked multiplication and balance additions.
transferFrom mutates allowance and balances with raw unchecked arithmetic.
transfer() uses msg.sender as the implicit source of the token movement.
msg.sender determines the allowance spender and the whitelist branch in ensure().
approve() writes allowance[msg.sender][_spender].
delegate() accepts requests only when msg.sender equals owner.
_mints() gates minting on a hardcoded msg.sender whitelist.
init() requires msg.sender to be the owner.
batchSend() requires msg.sender to be the owner.
setTradeAddress() requires msg.sender to be the owner.
The constructor assigns owner = msg.sender and grants it the full supply.
Constructor sets the privileged owner state variable.
Constructor mints the whole supply into balanceOf[msg.sender].
Constructor grants the UNI router an unlimited allowance on behalf of the owner.
_mints() increases balanceOf[spender] without updating totalSupply.
_mints() marks the spender as sellable in canSale, bypassing condition checks.
batchSend() debits the owner and credits each recipient in balanceOf.
setTradeAddress() rewrites the tradeAddress whitelist used by ensure().
init() writes _minSale from its token parameter.
init() writes _maxSale from its maxToken parameter.
init() writes _saleNum from its saleNum parameter.
condition() reads _onSaleNum[_from] to enforce the per-address sale count.
condition() compares _minSale against the transfer value.
condition() compares the transfer value against _maxSale.
condition() compares _onSaleNum[_from] against _saleNum.
transferFrom debits and credits balanceOf with unchecked subtraction and addition.
transferFrom decreases allowance[_from][msg.sender] after checking it.
ensure() treats owner as an unconditional whitelist entry allowing any transfer.
ensure() returns true for any address flagged in canSale, bypassing condition().
